Architecture.text:
Architecture
Two deployed applications, one calculation layer.
System Flow
Browser → Streamlit frontend → HTTPS API → FastAPI backend → validated datasets and Python calculations → page results → charts and tables.
For AI actions, the backend sends selected analysis context to LangChain and OpenRouter, then returns a checked response to the frontend. The default model is google/gemini-2.5-flash.
Responsibilities
frontend/: navigation, charts, tables, filters, staff sign-in and the API client. It does not import analysis or AI implementation code.
backend/: FastAPI routes, page services, dataset storage and AI orchestration. Deployed on Render.
core/: CSV validation, synthetic data generation, calculations and AI safeguards.
shared/: request and response models, filter definitions and access policy shared across the two applications.
Data and Calculation Rules
Eight related CSV files cover events, sponsors, sponsorships, registrations, sessions, engagement, leads and feedback. Validation checks columns, types, dates, identifiers and relationships before analysis. Filters are applied consistently across related tables.
Show-up rate uses confirmed registrations. NPS is a proxy derived from 1–5 ratings, not a standard 0–10 recommendation survey. Sponsor contract values are allocated evenly across the events each sponsor sponsored. Undefined rates are shown as unavailable rather than invented values.
Access and Privacy
The public demo uses synthetic data and hides uploads. Custom or uploaded datasets require staff OIDC sign-in and an approved email list. A shared BACKEND_API_TOKEN protects API routes except /health. The frontend sends it server-to-server; model API keys stay on the backend.
Portfolio chat and reports use computed aggregates. Feedback AI receives comment text after common contact details are redacted; real comments need review for remaining identifiers. Numerical checks reduce unsupported figures but do not replace human review.
Deployment and Limits
Streamlit Community Cloud hosts the frontend; Render hosts the backend. Dataset state is held in memory, so use one backend worker. Restarting the backend clears uploaded datasets. Persistent storage, audit trails and production retention controls need separate planning.
Repository README · Backend health endpoint

System Flow

Browser → Streamlit frontend → HTTPS API → FastAPI backend → validated datasets and Python calculations → page results → charts and tables.

For AI actions, the backend sends selected analysis context to LangChain and OpenRouter, then returns a checked response to the frontend. The default model is google/gemini-2.5-flash.

  • frontend/: navigation, charts, tables, filters, staff sign-in and the API client. It does not import analysis or AI implementation code.

  • backend/: FastAPI routes, page services, dataset storage and AI orchestration. Deployed on Render.

  • core/: CSV validation, synthetic data generation, calculations and AI safeguards.

  • shared/: request and response models, filter definitions and access policy shared across the two applications.

Data and Calculation Rules

Eight related CSV files cover events, sponsors, sponsorships, registrations, sessions, engagement, leads and feedback. Validation checks columns, types, dates, identifiers and relationships before analysis. Filters are applied consistently across related tables.

Show-up rate uses confirmed registrations. NPS is a proxy derived from 1–5 ratings, not a standard 0–10 recommendation survey. Sponsor contract values are allocated evenly across the events each sponsor sponsored. Undefined rates are shown as unavailable rather than invented values.

Access and Privacy

The public demo uses synthetic data and hides uploads. Custom or uploaded datasets require staff OIDC sign-in and an approved email list. A shared BACKEND_API_TOKEN protects API routes except /health. The frontend sends it server-to-server; model API keys stay on the backend.

Portfolio chat and reports use computed aggregates. Feedback AI receives comment text after common contact details are redacted; real comments need review for remaining identifiers. Numerical checks reduce unsupported figures but do not replace human review.

Deployment and Limits

Streamlit Community Cloud hosts the frontend; Render hosts the backend. Dataset state is held in memory, so use one backend worker. Restarting the backend clears uploaded datasets. Persistent storage, audit trails and production retention controls need separate planning.

Build Guide.text:
Build Guide
Before You Start
Use Python 3.12, Git and uv. Clone nagv/ConferAtlas. An OpenRouter key is optional for dashboards and required for AI calls. The repository includes a synthetic dataset; no real attendee data is needed to try it.
Recommended Build Path
Explore the experience. Start at Welcome, open Portfolio overview, then inspect an event, sponsor results, audience and feedback.
Install the project. Create the virtual environment and install requirements.txt using the commands in the Commands tab.
Configure AI if needed. Copy backend/.env.example to backend/.env. Set OPENROUTER_API_KEY and use OPENROUTER_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1. Keep keys out of Git.
Run both apps. Use run_local.py from the repository root. The API runs on port 8000 and the frontend on port 8501.
Validate the journey. Apply a filter, compare KPI cards and scorecards, inspect sponsor targets and download a CSV. Then try one grounded AI question and review its calculations.
Cloud Deployment
Deploy the backend from the repository root on Render with backend/requirements.txt and backend.main:app. Set BACKEND_API_TOKEN and any model key in Render’s environment. Leave CONFERATLAS_DATA_DIR unset for the built-in synthetic demo.
Deploy frontend/app.py on Streamlit Community Cloud. Its top-level Secrets need BACKEND_URL=https://conferatlas.onrender.com, the matching BACKEND_API_TOKEN, CONFERATLAS_PUBLIC_DEMO=true and CONFERATLAS_REQUIRE_AUTH=false. Reboot after changing deployment settings.
Check the Result
The health endpoint returns HTTP 200 and status ok.
All pages load, filters remain consistent and empty selections show a reset action.
Invalid datasets fail validation before analysis.
AI answers show their calculation evidence and handle missing keys or provider errors clearly.
Public demo mode hides uploads; custom data remains protected.
Use Initial Prompt as a short project brief and Refined Prompt as the implementation specification. Their conference analytics requirements replace the original stock-analysis template.

Build Guide

Before You Start

Use Python 3.12, Git and uv. Clone nagv/ConferAtlas. An OpenRouter key is optional for dashboards and required for AI calls. The repository includes a synthetic dataset; no real attendee data is needed to try it.

Recommended Build Path

  1. Explore the experience. Start at Welcome, open Portfolio overview, then inspect an event, sponsor results, audience and feedback.

  2. Install the project. Create the virtual environment and install requirements.txt using the commands in the Commands tab.

  3. Configure AI if needed. Copy backend/.env.example to backend/.env. Set OPENROUTER_API_KEY and use OPENROUTER_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1. Keep keys out of Git.

  4. Run both apps. Use run_local.py from the repository root. The API runs on port 8000 and the frontend on port 8501.

  5. Validate the journey. Apply a filter, compare KPI cards and scorecards, inspect sponsor targets and download a CSV. Then try one grounded AI question and review its calculations.

Cloud Deployment

Deploy the backend from the repository root on Render with backend/requirements.txt and backend.main:app. Set BACKEND_API_TOKEN and any model key in Render’s environment. Leave CONFERATLAS_DATA_DIR unset for the built-in synthetic demo.

Deploy frontend/app.py on Streamlit Community Cloud. Its top-level Secrets need BACKEND_URL=https://conferatlas.onrender.com, the matching BACKEND_API_TOKEN, CONFERATLAS_PUBLIC_DEMO=true and CONFERATLAS_REQUIRE_AUTH=false. Reboot after changing deployment settings.

Check the Result

  • The health endpoint returns HTTP 200 and status ok.

  • All pages load, filters remain consistent and empty selections show a reset action.

  • Invalid datasets fail validation before analysis.

  • AI answers show their calculation evidence and handle missing keys or provider errors clearly.

  • Public demo mode hides uploads; custom data remains protected.

Use Initial Prompt as a short project brief and Refined Prompt as the implementation specification. Their conference analytics requirements replace the original stock-analysis template.

THE GEN ACADEMY
Week 1, Code Track
ConferAtlas: Conference Intelligence
Code: GitHub repository
Data: Synthetic conference dataset
Demonstration: Watch demonstration
Turn conference data into a clearer story of impact.
Use Case Overview
Conference teams need to explain how events performed and what sponsors received. Registrations, session engagement, leads and attendee feedback are often spread across separate files. ConferAtlas brings them together to support event planning, sponsor reporting and renewal conversations.
Solution Description
ConferAtlas combines interactive Streamlit dashboards with a separate FastAPI backend. Python calculates the results; AI helps explain them. Users can compare events, inspect audience and feedback patterns, measure sponsor leads against targets, ask portfolio questions and prepare downloadable sponsor summaries.
Who It Serves
Event leaders and organisers review portfolio performance. Sponsorship teams prepare evidence for sponsors. Sponsors receive exported reports rather than app accounts. Public visitors can explore the built-in synthetic demo; real or uploaded data requires staff sign-in.
What You’ll Build
Portfolio and event dashboards with shared filters, KPI cards, charts and scorecards.
Sponsor performance and report views showing leads, targets, costs and audience context.
Audience and feedback analysis, with optional AI summaries and portfolio chat.
A separate data and AI API, shared contracts, validation and access controls.
Use Project Outline for the user flow and screen tour, Architecture for the system design, and Build Guide and Commands to run the project.

Project Outline.text:
Project Outline
Follow the evidence from a portfolio view to a sponsor-ready report.
User Flow
Welcome → Portfolio overview → Apply filters → Investigate an event → Review sponsor performance → Prepare and review a sponsor report → Export and share.
Audience insights and Feedback analyzer provide supporting evidence at any point. Ask the portfolio and AI insights are optional interpretation tools; users review the source calculations before sharing results.
Access path: public visitors explore synthetic data. Staff sign-in is required before uploaded or custom data can be shown. The public demo has no upload controls.

Flow Diagram

Screen Tour
Welcome: introduces the purpose, audience and starting points.
Portfolio overview: headline KPIs, trends, event comparison and downloadable scorecards.
Event drill-down: attendance, session capacity, engagement, sponsors and feedback for one event.
Sponsor performance / Sponsor report: leads against targets, source mix and cost per lead; sponsor-specific evidence and report preparation.
Audience insights / Feedback analyzer: attendee mix, returning visitors, ratings and comment themes.
Ask the portfolio / AI insights: grounded questions, event pitches and renewal briefs.
About: synthetic-data disclosure, metric definitions and AI privacy notes.
Suggested Review Journey
Open Portfolio overview and note the current scope.
Choose a date range or event type, then select Apply filters.
Inspect an event and compare its attendance, session ratings and leads.
Review sponsor results and select a sponsor for a focused report.
Use audience and feedback views to add context.
Review calculations and any AI draft; export the scorecard or report.
Application Screenshots
Captured from the deployed synthetic demo. Figures illustrate the demo and are not real event results.

Welcome — Platform Overview
The landing page introduces the conference intelligence platform and the public synthetic demo.



Portfolio Overview — Compare Event Results
The portfolio view combines attendance, satisfaction, sponsor revenue and lead metrics with event comparisons. All values shown use the built-in synthetic dataset.



Sponsor Performance — Review Sponsor Value
Review leads against target, cost per lead, booth visits and renewals before preparing a sponsor report. The screenshot uses synthetic demo data.
